title: Abd al-Rahman the Maghribi's Story of the Rukh

full_text:
Abd al-Rahman the Maghribi, an intrepid mariner from the shores of North Africa, appeared before the court of Harun al-Rashid carrying an astonishing curiosity: a translucent pipe or trough carved from a single bird’s quill, large enough to hold two skins of water!

When the Caliph marveled at the object, Abd al-Rahman related the perilous voyage on which he had obtained it:

'In my youth, our merchant vessel was blown off course by a furious hurricane into the uncharted southern waters of the Sea of China. After weeks of drift, we sighted a mountainous island rising from the azure waves. In the center of the island stood an enormous white dome, shining like polished alabaster, spanning fifty paces across and rising into the clouds.

Thinking it was the tomb of an ancient titan, my companions and I climbed the grassy slope. When we struck the dome with our pickaxes, it cracked, and we discovered with awe and dread that it was not stone at all, but the colossal egg of the legendary Rukh—the monstrous bird of the heavens that preys upon elephants!

Presently, the sky darkened as if a black thunderhead had blotted out the midday sun. Looking up, we beheld wings that spanned the horizon, each feather like a ship's sail, and eyes that burned like twin beacons. It was the parent Rukh returning to its nest!

Terrified, we scrambled back to our ship, hoisted all sail, and pulled with our oars. The giant bird circled the island, let out a cry that shook the sea, and flew toward the mountains. From the abandoned nest, I snatched this single quill fragment that had fallen from the egg’s down.

The Caliph held the massive quill in his hands, marveling at how frail human knowledge is before the infinite mysteries of the unexplored earth.'
moral: The boundless wonders of creation surpass human imagination, inspiring awe and humility.
